name: The Perfect Hire
pitch: One helpless cow, one little saucer, one instantly readable joke. The strongest candidate for a small store thumbnail.
tradeoff: Less sense of the wider world and the military chase.
logo: Cream inflated block lettering; a mint capture ring under the O becomes the brand symbol.
scene: ICONIC MINIMAL HERO. A huge pear-shaped cow floats upside down, diagonally through the central two-thirds of the cover, four tiny legs splayed, funny calm coral muzzle facing viewer. Tiny cobalt saucer above/right tugs it upward with a clean curved mint dotted trail; a detached farmer's amber straw hat follows far below as the only secondary gag. Rich flat deep petrol/navy background with extremely subtle painted tonal planes, NO landscape, no stars, no other characters. Monumental silhouette, lots of breathing room. Light cow and mint make three punchy graphic masses. The bespoke ivory title logo occupies bottom quarter, tightly stacked HUMAN / RESOURCES, rounded dimensional painted letters with subtle cobalt edge and small mint capture-ring counter in the O. Short soft cast shadows and mint reflected rimlight. Premium editorial restraint.

name: Personnel Department
pitch: Makes the title's HR joke explicit: abduction becomes recruitment. The most distinctive brand premise.
tradeoff: The paperwork metaphor puts less emphasis on action.
logo: A bold navy corporate seal, with a saucer-and-person capture symbol.
scene: DEADPAN RECRUITMENT CAMPAIGN. Warm ivory paper-like background, meticulously designed official personnel-file cover aesthetic, translated into the SAME painterly low-poly rendered game characters. Three large overlapping recruitment ID-card panels arranged on a playful diagonal: the center card shows a farmer being lifted out of his portrait aperture, arms hanging; left card a very round cow; right card sleepy robe resident clutching his nightcap. The small actual cobalt saucer hovers above this organized cast lineup and mint dotted suction lifts the farmer and his amber hat OUT OF THE CARDS. Cards simple ivory and sage without readable administrative tiny text, just small graphic lines. Top third enormous sophisticated navy logo HUMAN / RESOURCES as a rounded geometric stamped corporate seal with an original mint saucer/person icon and restrained coral stamp-like accent, no other text. Broad painted texture on characters, crisp graphic layout, subtle 3D card shadows. Feels like an alien HR department's unnervingly cheerful recruitment advertisement; do not depict an office or aliens.

name: Mass Recruitment
pitch: Turns the game's collecting loop into a big spiral of comic motion. Best for conveying abundance and momentum.
tradeoff: Needs careful simplification when cropped very small.
logo: An angled two-line wordmark pulled toward a mint orbital sweep.
scene: KINETIC OVERHEAD VORTEX. Entire cover viewed directly overhead over a broad sage farmland field. A large S-shaped spiral of MINT dotted capture trails sweeps from bottom-left around center up into the cobalt saucer at upper-right. Along that spiral float five individually legible comically posed recruits: upside-down pear cow dominant near center, flailing farmer with detached amber hat, cream sheep, salmon pig, sleepy navy-robed resident. Every character distinct and spaced, visually big, never a cluttered crowd. Tiny quiet terracotta barn roof and wheat bale cropped at outer corners only; one small navy tracked tank on the far lower edge shoots a restrained coral tracer that misses the orbit. Broad quiet terrain and strong circular eye movement. TITLE LOGO at upper-left, big two-line cream rounded forward-leaning wordmark HUMAN / RESOURCES with dark navy dimensional extrusion; a mint orbital swoosh sweeps through its baseline and visually leads into the composition. Energetic carefully art-directed cover with real painted game models, no photorealism.

name: The Night Shift
pitch: A sleepy suburban abduction becomes a quiet visual joke. Best for atmosphere and a warmer, more unusual tone.
tradeoff: Its calm mood undersells the game's faster action.
logo: Warm ivory moonlit lettering with a saucer halo.
scene: QUIET SUBURBAN NIGHT, CINEMATIC WIT. Low three-quarter street view at blue hour. Almost entire cover is a beautifully controlled deep slate-blue night sky above a small row of low-poly cream houses with coral and teal roofs and tiny warm amber windows along the lower fifth. A single sleepy resident in navy robe and mustard nightcap floats horizontally, slippered feet toward viewer and expression still half asleep, lifted from his front garden into a hovering cobalt saucer at upper-mid right; detached nightcap tassel expressive, one loose slipper floats behind. A narrow translucent mint spotlight and sparse mint dots form a graceful vertical column through the dark composition, picking out painted facets. Sage hedge, tiny curb and streetlamp. No military, no starfield clutter. Large title logo in upper quarter HUMAN / RESOURCES in warm ivory rounded bespoke lettering, slightly arched like a sleepy moon, small mint saucer halo hovering over the O; tasteful satin painted dimensionality. Elegant asymmetric negative space and one brilliant light event. Keep this specific game's comic miniature identities, not realism.

name: Occupational Hazard
pitch: Pitches the game as a comic chase. Best for immediate excitement and showing the military threat.
tradeoff: The busiest and most action-led option.
logo: Heavy cream action lettering with a coral offset and mint beam underline.
scene: COMIC ACTION BLOCKBUSTER with bold diagonal ground-level perspective. HUGE foreshortened pear-shaped ivory/black cow in near foreground flying belly-up toward camera, little coral muzzle and four silly legs clearly visible, a terrified-but-funny farmer clings to its rear ankle while amber hat spins away. The cobalt saucer banks above/behind at top left, mint lights blazing, pulling both along a sweeping mint dotted path. Farther below in a small sage farm lane, a single navy TRACKED TANK and open jeep chase with coral chevrons; one red-tipped missile arcs across the lower midground and is neatly intercepted by a tiny mint spark, NO explosions or violence. Barn and fence angle backwards to exaggerate speed, warm painted gouache facets against cool slate shadows. Navy sky as clean dark ground for large cream title logo across top HUMAN / RESOURCES, chunky tightly stacked italic rounded geometric letters with restrained coral offset shadow and a mint beam underline. Center hero and logo remain unmistakable even at small size. Joyful slapstick not angry aggressive faces, no cinema credits.

name: Field Work
pitch: Uses absence as the joke: a giant saucer shadow, one farmer, and his hat. Best for a striking, restrained poster.
tradeoff: More mysterious; says less about collecting animals.
logo: Wide navy field lettering with a crop-circle emblem.
scene: CONCEPTUAL NEGATIVE-SPACE POSTER. Direct straight-down orthographic view of a single softly hand-painted sage-green farm field. An enormous crisp dark petrol-blue SHADOW in the recognizable silhouette of the game's saucer occupies most of the middle, tilted diagonally. The actual small cobalt saucer is visible at upper-right, its height implied by the oversized shadow. At the very center of the saucer shadow, a tiny but perfectly readable farmer in amber hat looks upward with arms spread; his amber straw hat is lifting away just above him on a few mint capture dots. One cream cow stands OUTSIDE the shadow at lower-left, watching, making an understated joke. Minimal tan dirt path and one piece of wooden fence at edge, no dense scenery. Huge premium typographic title lockup HUMAN / RESOURCES spans top fifth in deep navy with restrained ivory keyline; custom rounded lettering integrated with a small crop-circle emblem that can function independently. Use strong light/dark shape design, unusual precise framing, poster-art confidence. Shadow physically simplified for impact, all actual objects visibly hand-painted low-poly 3D, avoid flat vector appearance.

name: Employee of the Month
pitch: Gives the game a mascot: a cow taking recruitment far too seriously. Best for character recognition and comic personality.
tradeoff: Could make players expect the cow to be the protagonist.
logo: A confident navy badge with ivory lettering and a mint orbit.
scene: DEADPAN HERO PORTRAIT. A beautifully lit enormous pear-shaped cow stands front-facing, filling central two-thirds of warm ivory poster, huge rounded belly, tiny indigo-black head/ears, coral muzzle, short matchstick legs, a supremely blank dignified expression. On its chest a simple small navy-and-mint rosette with a tiny saucer pictogram, no readable words. Behind its head a circular MINT capture ring looks like an absurd official portrait halo. Upper right a tiny actual cobalt saucer floats, revealing that the cow is being recruited; its hooves are lifted just a little above the ground. Bottom-left at tiny scale the farmer in amber hat looks up, hands on hips, as if passed over for the award. Broad gouache cream/ochre brush patches on cow's low-poly form, navy-indigo painted black patches, soft warm keylight. Title logo HUMAN / RESOURCES at bottom in a big navy rounded geometric badge with cream letters, a mint orbit stroke along one corner. Symmetric dignified portrait composition with humorous asymmetry from small UFO and farmer. No office scenery, no other text, no realism, no shiny toy.

name: Roadside Attraction
pitch: Turns the desert setting into a strange destination worth visiting. Best for a memorable world and a vintage poster feel.
logo: A custom roadside-sign silhouette with ivory lettering and a cobalt saucer finial.
scene: RETRO ROADSIDE DESTINATION POSTER rendered with hand-painted LOW-POLY 3D miniature forms. Portrait composition: a bold original roadside-sign-shaped logo fills upper third, cream rounded HUMAN / RESOURCES lettering on a deep navy sculpted sign plaque, mint trim and a small cobalt UFO as its sign finial. Below, an empty plum-grey highway curves deeply into warm ochre desert, huge simple mauve/blush faceted mesas left and right, a few dusty sage cacti, tiny rust-roof service canopy lower-left. At bend, the ACTUAL cobalt saucer has paused low over the road and lifts a cow and amber-hatted farmer in a restrained mint capture field like an absurd roadside attraction. Strong golden afternoon and cool lavender painted shadows, clear restrained local palette. Highway and two visible recruits large enough to read; sign and world form a unified cover, no extra captions, no written route numbers. Retro travel-poster composition and warm/cool blocks but the actual subjects are clearly the selected tactile painterly low-poly game art, not flat vintage illustration or realistic desert.

name: Upward Mobility
pitch: Builds a clean visual rhythm out of recruits rising toward the saucer. Best for portrait formats and communicating the upward pull.
logo: Tall stacked ivory lettering with a rising mint baseline.
scene: HIGHLY GRAPHIC VERTICAL RECRUITMENT LADDER. Deep cobalt-to-petrol subtly painted backdrop, no landscape. Bottom-to-top sequence of exactly four LARGE separated floating game characters, ascending in a gentle stepped zigzag: salmon pig low left, cream sheep lower right, wide pear cow center left, flailing amber-hatted farmer center right, all caught in one elegant narrow winding mint dotted suction trail that terminates at a small cobalt saucer near the top center. They rotate by distinct funny angles; not piled on one another, not standing on a tower. An isolated straw hat floats nearest the UFO as final punctuation. A dramatic long vertical upward movement with lots of navy breathing room between shapes. Warm hand-painted brush planes on the low-poly models, short mint rimlights and no excessive bloom. Logo takes BOTTOM quarter, enormous bespoke ivory HUMAN / RESOURCES stacked tightly and rising slightly from left to right, a single mint ascending underline and a small capture-dot symbol, readable letters and professional optical balance. Bold editorial mobile cover, instantly legible silhouettes, no extra wording or UI.

name: World’s Best Employer
pitch: Puts farm, suburb, and desert into one tiny world to harvest. Best for showing scope and supporting a lasting game identity.
tradeoff: Its world metaphor is less literal than the gameplay.
logo: Broad ivory lettering with a planetary capture-ring crest.
scene: TINY WORLD, BIG AMBITION. A charming floating SMALL SPHERICAL MINIATURE PLANET takes central half of portrait poster, constructed in the selected hand-painted low-poly style, three readable continuous biomes: sage farmland with one cream terracotta-roof barn and wheat bale, slate suburban street with two tiny cream coral/teal houses, warm ochre desert with mauve rocks and sage cacti. Planet not cutaway, no diorama box. A single cobalt saucer sweeps in an orbit above/left and plucks a LARGE funny upside-down ivory cow and one amber-hatted farmer away from its surface along an elegant mint dotted arc. The recruits deliberately oversized enough to read, no alien pilot, no armies. Background broad deep navy with NO busy stars, restrained mint ring wraps the lower planet like an acquisitive logo gesture. Title HUMAN / RESOURCES very large ivory rounded custom lettering in upper quarter, broad confident two-line lockup, small planetary capture-ring crest integrated into the O without breaking readability. Funny cosmic corporate ambition, premium 3D painted key art, beautiful warm local biome colours and mint accents, no space-opera seriousness.
